card.name: Linking words before lab-marker thresholds
card.fires_on: Small linking words and punctuation (with, of, than, to, and/or, comma) inside statin-type myopathy and liver-injury descriptions, just before a lab value such as creatine kinase, ALT/AST or creatinine, or a severity outcome.

modes.label: Muscle symptoms to CK
modes.description: Word linking muscle pain or weakness to an elevated creatine kinase value.
modes.example: unexplained muscle weakness or pain<< with>> a serum creatine kinase [CK]

modes.label: Liver or kidney thresholds
modes.description: Word or symbol just before a numeric cutoff or lab marker in liver or kidney warnings.
modes.example: Elevations of ALT or AST (less<< than>> three times ULN) may occur in

modes.label: Severity grading
modes.description: Linking word in a toxicity grade definition leading toward hospitalization or life-threatening outcomes.
modes.example: Severe or medically significant but<< not>> immediately life-threatening; hospitalization or prolong

card.writes: It pushes toward serious-outcome words like hospital, mortality, permanent and incapacitating, and away from unrelated junk tokens.
card.plain: It marks the small connecting words in warnings about muscle or liver damage, right before a lab value or serious outcome is named.
